title: Document evidence, requested constituent, literal answer
goal: Read the correct evidence, then return exactly the constituent requested by the question
guidance:
Use the supplied document image as evidence. Resolve the requested relation, locate its supporting field or sentence, and select the requested constituent before transcribing it. Evidence context and the answer are different: evidence_text may include a full row or sentence, while answer contains only what the question asks for.

Locate by role and layout. Distinguish sender from recipient, supplier from customer, and an entity from its address or department. In tables, intersect the correct row, column and period. For maxima or minima, identify the requested measure and its units, then compare that same measure across eligible rows. Counts and rates are different measures. A crop must remain anchored to the relevant label and row in the original page.

Choose the constituent by the question, not by a preference for short or long answers. A role or job title is distinct from the person's employer or affiliation; include the latter only when requested or integral to the title. A why-question asks for the stated cause, without repeating the effect already supplied in the question. A quantity retains bounds and qualifiers such as more than, less than, approximately or a range; omit the surrounding description of what is being counted. A name is the complete named entity, not sentence-introducing prepositions or articles unless they belong to the name. Preserve coordinated words and scope qualifiers within a formal heading; do not shorten it to a familiar brand. Do not append adjacent addresses, divisions or subtitles. An identifier and its descriptive heading are separate constituents; a title question can require the heading itself.

Transcribe the selected constituent literally. Preserve singular/plural, digits, precision, internal punctuation, currency signs, measurement units and semantic qualifiers that belong to the value. A neighboring field label, page ornament or unused printed form slot is not part of the value; a blank slot is not zero. Do not append a substance or item name when only its amount was requested. Do not expand abbreviations, normalize a source phrase to a dictionary definition, or repair an unfamiliar name from memory. Use ordinary straight ASCII quotes and apostrophes for source quotation marks, without adding new quotation marks.

If a tiny, handwritten or ambiguous character would change the answer, inspect its field at a larger scale when available. Use its label and the same-source row context to confirm relevance; compare strokes with nearby writing instead of completing a plausible word or date. Clear evidence needs no repeated verification. After selecting and reading the constituent, submit it faithfully without a new paraphrase or shortening pass. Return only <answer>...</answer>.
